explanation: The patriarch of the people of Israel and founder of the Hebrew nation, with whom God made a covenant.
A title often used for God in the Old Testament, referring to his sovereignty and authority.
A place near Hebron where Abraham settled and built an altar to the Lord. It was here that God visited him in chapter 18.
An important value in Middle Eastern cultures, including Abraham's time. Showing hospitality means welcoming others well and caring for their needs.
Heavenly beings who serve as God's messengers and carry out his will. In this story, three men visit Abraham, and they are later identified as angels.
Two cities that, according to the Bible, were destroyed by God because of their wickedness and immorality.
The concept refers to acting rightly and in accordance with God's will and moral standards. Abraham asks God to spare Sodom and Gomorrah if there are righteous people there.
Abraham's nephew, who lived in Sodom and was rescued by the angels before the city's destruction.
